text:
Emma Park: Quick design review — attaching screenshots of the compact invite flow and a couple of variants for the SSO toggle placement. Need feedback on copy and a11y before we freeze for dev.
Raj Patel: Nice. Can you paste the primary flows? hard to read in image. TL;DR: which one is our default?
Emma Park: Default is Variant B — SSO toggle inline under Org settings header, invite drawer opens from right, roles matrix condensed.
Santiago Gomez: I like Variant B for desktop. Two quick notes: 1) roles matrix needs a clear keyboard focus state for each cell, 2) the condensed rows hide secondary perms — we should have a "details" chevron.
Mia Chen: Accessibility: make sure the SSO toggle has an aria-describedby that explains "SSO enforced means users must sign in via SSO". Also color contrast on the read-only badge is low.
Jules (design): Copy nits: "Invite members" vs "Add teammates" — product prefers "Invite members" per previous research. Also propose microcopy under SSO toggle: "When enabled, users must authenticate through your SSO provider." shorter:  "SSO required for org sign-in."
Raj Patel: For the invite flow: can we show a validation inline for duplicate emails? Current mock shows a bulk paste area but no immediate feedback. Duplicate or invalid should flag before submit.
Emma Park: Good call — add inline chips with error states. Also thinking about an "Upload CSV" fallback for larger teams.
Santiago Gomez: Audit log nav: second screenshot shows flat list. Request: add quick filters at top (by action type, by user, by time range) + sticky column headers. Also allow "group by user" toggle so SREs can see sessionings.
Mia Chen: Keyboard nav on audit log: table rows should be arrow-key navigable, and each row's action menu must be reachable via Enter/Space. Use role="grid" and proper aria-row and aria-colindex.
Jules (design): UX question: where do we surface SSO enforcement in the invite drawer? Inline note next to role selector or only in org-level banner? If we put it inline, it might cause noise for small invites.
Emma Park: Proposed compromise: show a subtle inline hint only when SSO is enabled org-wide, and a prominent banner if SSO enforcement will block invited users from accepting (e.g., invites sent to non-SSO domains). Example copy: "Note: these users must use SSO to sign in."
Raj Patel: Implementation note: backend will return a flag `sso_enforced` and `domain_mismatch` for preview recipients. Frontend should render the banner if domain_mismatch == true.
Mia Chen: Also ensure the invite drawer fields have accessible labels for screen readers — name/email input should announce validation: "Email invalid" / "Email already invited".
Santiago Gomez: On roles matrix: mobile collapsed rows — prefer a stacked list view with primary role on left and permission count on right. Avoid horizontal scrolling.
Jules (design): Tooltip text for permissions: keep short, avoid sentences. Eg: "Can manage API keys." instead of "This role allows users to manage API keys across the org, including creating and revoking keys."
Emma Park: Thanks team. Action items: Jules to update copy and hint placements, Mia to add a11y checklist bits (aria roles + focus), Raj to spec API flags and validation payloads, Santiago to supply responsive matrix patterns. I'll re-upload updated mocks by EOD.
deploy-bot: deploy-preview/roles-invite-ui created — view at https://staging.redwood.ai/preview/roles-invite-ui (preview expires in 48h)
Raj Patel: quick Q — can we A/B test the banner severity? mild vs prominent? want metrics on invite acceptance.
Emma Park: Yes — add a variant flag for canary. We'll track accept_rate and support tickets per cohort.
Mia Chen: One last a11y nit: make sure the SSO toggle state is programmatically determinable (aria-checked). Also document keyboard shortcut to open invite drawer ("g i"?) in the help center.
Emma Park: Perfect. Closing this thread after mocks get updated. :rocket:
